title: The Last Cipher Anew
premise: Lior Thornbury has built her career on being forgettable: an interpreter who hears everything and reports only what suits her handlers. When a stranger named Vasik repays a favor she never performed, she learns her fabricated testimony years ago condemned an innocent man—and that the man's family now runs the syndicate bankrolling the peace summit. To survive the week, Lior must choose between exposing her own perjury and letting the syndicate's bought delegates sign away a nation. In the end, she broadcasts her confession during the closing session, trading her invisibility and freedom for the summit's collapse and a slimmer, honest chance at peace.
about_author: Q. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in delegation rooms across three continents before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about the people history forgets: translators, couriers, and witnesses.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Days before the summit, a stranger named Vasik corners her with proof of a favor she never performed—and a debt with interest. He reveals her old testimony helped convict an innocent man, Aldric Venn, whose family now funds the summit's security. Lior realizes her invisibility was always someone else's design. Emotional beat: dread masquerading as routine.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with a Vasik interlude. Vasik's demand: she must misinterpret the closing session to bury a syndicate clause. Lior digs into Venn's case and finds her handlers manufactured her testimony to protect the same delegates now selling out the peace process. Her handler, Sorrel, warns her off with chilling gentleness. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning you were always complicit.

chapters.title: Every Word a Weapon
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Sorrel POV. Lior attempts to leak the clause through a delegate, but Vasik intercepts it—his loyalty was to the Venn family all along, and the debt was a trap to place her inside the room. Sorrel orders her detained; Lior escapes through the summit's translation booths as delegates arrive. Emotional beat: betrayal on every side, and the cold clarity that follows it.

chapters.title: The Last Cipher
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, climax and resolution. In the closing session, instead of the scripted mistranslation, Lior renders every clause truthfully—then reads her own confession into the official record, naming Sorrel and the syndicate. The summit collapses; the Venns' leverage dies with it; Vasik walks away, debt settled. Lior surrenders to the police, finally visible. Emotional beat: ruin as release—the price of survival finally paid.
